message.content:
**London’s official time‑zone**

| Period | Standard abbreviation | Offset from UTC |
|--------|-----------------------|------------------|
| **Winter / Non–daylight‑saving period** | GMT (Greenwich Mean Time) | UTC ± 00:00 |
| **Summer / Daylight‑saving period** | BST (British Standard Time) | UTC ± 01:00 |

### How it works

* London follows the *Europe/London* entry in the IANA/Olson time‑zone database.  
* During most of the year (roughly late October → early March), clocks run on Greenwich Mean Time (GMT).  
* From the last Sunday in March until the last Sunday in October, Britain observes British Summer Time (BST), moving clocks forward one hour so they read UTC+1.

So if you’re looking up “what time zone is London?” – it’s **Europe/London**, switching between GMT (UTC+0) and BST (UTC+1) depending on the season.
